items.name: Proto-Indo-European (PIE)
items.desc: The reconstructed linguistic ancestor of over 400 languages spoken by nearly 3 billion people today.

children.note: Grimm's Law consonant shifts
Italic branch in Italian peninsula
Mycenaean & Ancient Greek branch
Sanskrit, Avestan and Persian branch
Slavic and Baltic language trunk

items.name: Proto-Afroasiatic
items.desc: One of the oldest phyla on earth; gave birth to Ancient Egyptian, Semitic (Akkadian, Arabic, Hebrew), and Berber.

children.note: Earliest written hieroglyphic branch
Triconsonantal root Semitic lineage

items.name: Proto-Sino-Tibetan
items.desc: Ancestral language giving rise to the Sinitic (Chinese) languages and Tibeto-Burman families.

children.note: Oracle bone and Bronze inscription Sinitic trunk

items.name: Sumerian
items.script: Cuneiform (First true writing system in history)
items.desc: Invented wedge-shaped cuneiform writing on clay tablets in southern Mesopotamia; completely isolated from all known families.

items.name: Ancient Egyptian
items.desc: Recorded over 3,000 continuous years of writing from Old Kingdom pyramid texts to Coptic Christian manuscripts.

parents.note: Oldest recorded Afroasiatic language

children.note: Proto-Sinaitic script adapted Egyptian hieroglyphs into first phonetic alphabet

items.name: Proto-Semitic
items.desc: Origin of the triconsonantal root system (e.g. k-t-b for writing) and Semitic phonology.

parents.note: Levant / Arabian peninsula branch

children.note: East Semitic Mesopotamian branch in cuneiform
Northwest Semitic maritime alphabet origin
Central Semitic peninsular branch

items.name: Phoenician
items.script: Phoenician Abjad (Ancestor of nearly all modern alphabets)
items.speakers: Extinct (Punic in Carthage until 6th c. CE)
items.desc: Maritime traders who popularized the 22-letter phonetic abjad, which directly gave birth to Greek, Latin, Cyrillic, Aramaic, Hebrew, and Arabic scripts.

parents.note: Canaanite coastal language
Phonetic script derived from Proto-Sinaitic glyphs

children.note: Greeks adapted Phoenician letters, inventing true vowel glyphs (Alpha, Epsilon, etc.)
Aramaic script evolved from Phoenician abjad

items.name: Ancient Greek
items.desc: Language of Homer, Plato, Aristotle, and Euclid; foundation of Western philosophy, mathematics, logic, and scientific vocabulary.

parents.note: Hellenic migration into Balkan peninsula
Adopted Phoenician alphabet and added explicit vowel letters

children.note: Western Greek alphabet adapted by Etruscans into Latin alphabet
Koine Greek evolved into Byzantine and Modern Greek

items.name: Latin (Classical)
items.desc: Language of the Roman Republic and Empire; survived as Europe's universal scientific and literary lingua franca for 2,000 years and birthed the Romance languages.

parents.note: Italic branch in Latium along the Tiber river
Alphabet adopted via Cumae Greek & Etruscan mediation

children.note: Vulgar Latin with Gaulish Celtic substrate & Frankish Germanic superstrate
Iberian Vulgar Latin with Mozarabic Arabic influence
Tuscan dialect direct literary descendant of Latin

items.name: Proto-Germanic
items.desc: Defined by Grimm's Law and Verner's Law of systematic consonant shifts; ancestor of English, German, Dutch, and Scandinavian languages.

parents.note: Jastorf culture and Nordic Bronze Age branch

children.note: North Sea Germanic Ingvaeonic dialects of Angles, Saxons, and Jutes
High German consonant shift branch

items.name: Old English (Anglo-Saxon)
items.script: Anglo-Saxon Futhorc Runes -> Insular Latin script
items.desc: Inflected Germanic language of Beowulf; heavily influenced by Old Norse during Danelaw Viking settlements.

parents.note: Settlement of Britain by Germanic tribes after Roman collapse

children.note: 1066 Norman Conquest fused Anglo-Saxon grammar with 10,000+ Norman French / Latin words

items.name: Modern English
items.desc: A unique hybrid: West Germanic core grammatical structure fused with massive Norman French and Latin lexical layers; international language of computing, aviation, and science.

parents.note: Core syntax, common verbs, prepositions, and grammatical backbone
Norman Conquest (1066) injected court, law, culinary, and military vocabulary
Renaissance influx of scholarly and scientific technical terms

items.name: Old Chinese (Archaic Sinitic)
items.script: Oracle Bone Script -> Bronze Inscriptions -> Seal Script
items.desc: Language of the Shang and Zhou dynasties; Shijing (Classic of Poetry) and I Ching; phonologically non-tonal with consonant clusters.

parents.note: Central Plains Neolithic settlement

children.note: Qieyun rhyming dictionary and tonal phonology under Sui & Tang dynasties

items.name: Middle Chinese
items.speakers: Extinct Classical (Evolved into modern Sinitic varieties)
items.desc: The Tang dynasty prestige language; phonological baseline recorded in the Qieyun rhyming dictionary; source of Sino-Japanese (Kanji), Sino-Korean (Hanja), and Sino-Vietnamese loanwords.

parents.note: Evolution through Warring States and Han dynasty Chinese

children.note: Northern Chinese variety, becoming Standard Chinese
Southern Yue branch retaining Middle Chinese final stop consonants (-p, -t, -k)

items.name: Standard Mandarin Chinese
items.desc: Prestige dialect based on Beijing phonology; tonal language (4 tones); official language of China and Taiwan.

parents.note: Phonological simplification of Middle Chinese in northern China
